audience: Businesses weighing new debt vs existing revenue
objective: Help business owners understand the difference between borrowing against future income and advancing revenue already earned.

slides.headline: Invoice Finance vs Business Loan
slides.subheadline: New debt, or revenue you've already earned?

slides.headline: What's the real difference?
slides.body: A business loan is new debt, assessed against your overall revenue and repaid over an agreed term. Invoice finance is an advance against unpaid invoices you've already issued — it isn't new debt in the same sense, and the amount available typically scales with your invoicing activity.

caption:
If your cash-flow gap comes from waiting on customers rather than needing new capital altogether, the right tool might not be a loan at all.

A business loan is new debt assessed against overall revenue. Invoice finance advances money against invoices you've already issued, typically scaling with your invoicing activity rather than requiring a fresh application each time.
